topics.name: react-fundamentals
facts: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces developed by Meta
React uses a virtual DOM to efficiently update the real DOM
JSX is a syntax extension that looks like HTML but compiles to React.createElement calls
Components are the building blocks of React applications — they are reusable pieces of UI
Functional components are JavaScript functions that return JSX
Props are read-only inputs passed to components from parent to child
State is mutable data managed within a component using useState hook
useState returns an array with the current state value and a setter function
useEffect runs side effects after render — for data fetching, subscriptions, DOM manipulation
The dependency array in useEffect controls when the effect re-runs
Hooks must be called at the top level of a component, never inside loops or conditions
useContext provides a way to pass data through the component tree without prop drilling
useRef creates a mutable reference that persists across renders without causing re-renders
useMemo memoizes expensive computations to avoid recalculating on every render
useCallback memoizes function references to prevent unnecessary child re-renders
Keys help React identify which items have changed in a list — use stable unique IDs
React fragments (<>...</>) let you group elements without adding extra DOM nodes
Conditional rendering uses &&, ternary operators, or if statements to show/hide elements
Event handlers in React use camelCase naming like onClick, onChange, onSubmit
Controlled components have their form state managed by React state, not the DOM

topics.name: typescript-basics
facts: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript
Type annotations are written with a colon after the variable name: let name: string
Interfaces define the shape of objects with required and optional properties
Type aliases can create union types, intersection types, and complex type expressions
Generics allow functions and components to work with any type while preserving type safety
The 'any' type disables type checking — avoid it when possible
The 'unknown' type is safer than 'any' because you must narrow it before use
Type narrowing uses typeof, instanceof, or custom type guards to refine types
Optional chaining (?.) safely accesses nested properties without throwing on null/undefined
Nullish coalescing (??) provides a default value only when the left side is null or undefined
Enums define a set of named constants — prefer const enums or union types for better output
The 'as' keyword performs type assertions — use sparingly, it bypasses type checking
Readonly<T> makes all properties of T immutable
Partial<T> makes all properties of T optional
Pick<T, K> creates a type with only the specified keys from T
Omit<T, K> creates a type with all keys from T except the specified ones
Record<K, V> creates an object type with keys K and values V
ReturnType<T> extracts the return type of a function type
tsconfig.json controls compiler options like strict mode, target, and module resolution
Strict mode enables strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, and other safety checks

topics.name: nextjs-fundamentals
facts: Next.js is a React framework for production with built-in routing, rendering, and optimization
Pages are React components exported from files in the pages/ or app/ directory
App Router (Next.js 13+) uses file-system based routing with layout.tsx, page.tsx, loading.tsx
Server Components render on the server and send HTML to the client — no client JavaScript needed
Client Components use 'use client' directive and run in the browser with full interactivity
Static generation (SSG) pre-renders pages at build time for maximum performance
Server-side rendering (SSR) generates pages on each request for dynamic content
Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) updates static pages after deployment without full rebuild
API routes in Next.js let you build backend endpoints alongside your frontend
Middleware runs before requests complete — useful for auth, redirects, and header modification
Image optimization with next/image provides automatic resizing, lazy loading, and WebP conversion
next/link enables client-side navigation with prefetching for instant page transitions
Environment variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are exposed to the browser
next.config.js configures webpack, redirects, headers, and other build settings
Dynamic imports with next/dynamic load components only when needed for code splitting
getServerSideProps runs on each request for pages that need fresh data
getStaticProps runs at build time for pages that can be pre-rendered
getStaticPaths defines which dynamic routes to pre-render at build time
Vercel is the company behind Next.js and provides optimized hosting
Edge runtime runs code at the CDN edge for lower latency globally

topics.name: tailwind-css
facts: Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom designs
Utility classes like 'flex', 'p-4', 'text-lg' compose directly in HTML without writing custom CSS
Responsive prefixes (sm:, md:, lg:, xl:) apply styles at specific breakpoints
Dark mode with 'dark:' prefix applies styles when the user prefers dark color scheme
Hover, focus, active states use prefixes like 'hover:', 'focus:', 'active:'
The config file (tailwind.config.js) customizes colors, spacing, fonts, and breakpoints
Arbitrary values like 'w-[300px]' or 'bg-[#bada55]' allow one-off custom values
JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler generates only the CSS classes you actually use
The 'group' utility styles children based on parent state with 'group-hover:'
The 'peer' utility styles siblings based on a peer element's state
Container queries with '@container' enable component-level responsive design
Tailwind's typography plugin provides prose classes for rich text content
Forms plugin resets form elements to a consistent cross-browser baseline
Aspect ratio plugin provides fixed aspect ratio containers
Line clamp plugin truncates text to a specific number of lines
CSS Grid utilities (grid, grid-cols-N, col-span-N) create complex grid layouts
Flexbox utilities (flex, items-center, justify-between) handle most layout needs
Spacing scale uses a consistent 4px-based system: p-1=4px, p-4=16px, p-8=32px
Color opacity utilities like 'bg-red-500/50' set background color at 50% opacity
The 'space-y-N' and 'space-x-N' utilities add consistent spacing between child elements

topics.name: testing
facts: Vitest is a Vite-native testing framework compatible with Jest's API
Unit tests verify individual functions or components in isolation
Integration tests verify that multiple units work together correctly
React Testing Library tests components from the user's perspective, not implementation details
render() from RTL renders a component into a virtual DOM for testing
screen.getByText() finds elements by their text content
screen.getByRole() finds elements by their ARIA role — preferred method
screen.getByTestId() finds elements by data-testid attribute — use as last resort
fireEvent simulates browser events like click, change, submit
userEvent (from @testing-library/user-event) simulates realistic user interactions
waitFor waits for assertions to pass within a timeout — useful for async operations
Mock functions (vi.fn()) track calls and control return values in tests
describe() groups related tests together for organization
beforeEach() runs setup code before each test in a describe block
afterEach() runs cleanup code after each test
test.todo() marks tests that need to be written later
test.skip() temporarily skips a test without deleting it
Code coverage measures what percentage of code is executed during tests
Snapshot testing captures rendered output and alerts on unexpected changes
End-to-end tests with Playwright or Cypress test the full application in a real browser

topics.name: react-patterns
facts: Presentational components focus on how things look, container components on how things work
Higher-Order Components (HOCs) are functions that take a component and return a new component
Render props share code between components using a prop whose value is a function
Compound components work together as a group — like Select/Option or Tabs/TabPanel
Custom hooks extract reusable stateful logic from components
The Context API provides a way to share values between components without prop drilling
Error boundaries catch JavaScript errors in child components and display fallback UI
Portals render children into a DOM node outside the parent component hierarchy
Lazy loading with React.lazy and Suspense splits code and shows fallback during loading
The useReducer hook manages complex state logic with actions and a reducer function
Immer simplifies immutable state updates by letting you write mutable-looking code
Zustand is a lightweight state management library with a simple hook-based API
React Query (TanStack Query) manages server state with caching, refetching, and mutations
Debouncing delays function execution until after a pause in calls — good for search inputs
Throttling limits function execution to at most once per time period — good for scroll handlers
Optimistic updates show the expected result immediately before the server confirms
Composition over inheritance — prefer composing components rather than extending classes
The children prop is special — anything between opening and closing tags becomes children
ForwardRef passes a ref through a component to a child DOM element
useImperativeHandle customizes the ref value exposed to parent components
